scope: Independent ST/SB native craft review only; no generation, display changes or mutation of frozen comparison board.

attempts.inspection: Actual complete native image via view_image detail original
observations: Strong adult expression, two grips and grounded opposing stances communicate a loaded first contact.
Cream hammer rim/side meets the bracer; the flat orange striking face is turned toward the viewer. Orange chip remains visible.
Marked foreground arm reads as Bellguard anatomical right; the plan specifies left.
limitations_and_failures: Side mismatch undermines continuity into ST02, even though the local contact is readable.
Small floor mottling and armor facets are present; no reflection carpet.
attempts.verdict: Reviewable action; anatomical-side and striking-surface caveats.

attempts.inspection: Actual complete native image via view_image detail original
observations: Same readable loaded contact, grin, separate legs and continuous turquoise shaft are preserved.
The ring now wraps further around the raised guard, but the elbow/upper-arm chain still does not clearly cross the chest from the anatomical left shoulder.
Floor appears broader and quieter than primary; no glossy repaint.
limitations_and_failures: Cannot certify left-arm repair: the foreground marked arm still visually reads as the right-side arm. This is an anatomical tracing uncertainty, not proof of an extra limb.
The cream rim still contacts the guard instead of flat orange striking face.
attempts.verdict: Partial/local improvement; requested side repair remains unverified.

attempts.inspection: Actual complete native image via view_image detail original
observations: Strong close foreshortened threat: huge unmarked fist passes above Tavi, whose expression changes from grin to concentration.
Marked rear arm clearly reads as anatomical left, with right arm extended in the punch. Two hammer grips, one continuous shaft and chipped orange face remain readable.
The low crouch, near knee and separate rear foot provide a coherent evasion path.
limitations_and_failures: Compared with ST01 primary/repair, the ring seems to change anatomical side; primary-to-repair topology remains ambiguous.
Hammer chip has enlarged and cream head cracking increased; plausible development but exact damage continuity is not preserved.
Ground and armor contain more small mottled marks than the quieter ST01 repair; keep any finish source-preserving.
attempts.verdict: Locally strong counter/evasion beat; sequence side/damage caveats.

attempts.inspection: Actual complete native image via view_image detail original
observations: Source palm, connected incoming orange path, bronze spearhead contact and upward turn are readable.
Two hand grips and separate full-body stances remain clear in warm outlined drawing.
limitations_and_failures: Cape is already burned despite setup occurring before damage in beat2.
Fire edge has many flame tongues; still a single dominant path rather than a particle cloud.
attempts.verdict: Premature damage makes setup continuity fail.

attempts.inspection: Actual complete native image via view_image detail original
observations: Cape restored to whole red cloth; source, bronze contact, upward fire turn, faces and two grips preserved.
Broad cream floor, strong cool/warm costume contrast and distinct Sunbreak drawing remain.
limitations_and_failures: The leading turn continues beyond frame, so its full endpoint is not shown; acceptable for setup, not proof of a return-path resolution.
attempts.verdict: Observed cape-timing repair succeeds without a newly obvious structural regression.

attempts.inspection: Actual complete native image via view_image detail original
observations: Expressive face, twisting torso and low charred cape communicate a dangerous counter and cost.
Caster and open palm remain visible at left; warm drawing and recognizable costumes continue.
limitations_and_failures: A second bronze pointed spearhead appears at the lower shaft end, in addition to the upper-right head. This changes the previously single-head weapon.
Both upper and lower heads appear to contact active fire. High fire has not faded; low defense is already touching the pulse instead of missing under a raised point.
Incoming low pulse is hidden behind torso/cape for much of its route; the large foreground flame may read as already passing the fighter.
Floor small mottling has returned somewhat, although broad shadow hierarchy survives.
attempts.verdict: Structural and causal repair warranted; do not treat visual excitement as successful beat2.

cross_frame_priority: Keep the orange mark on one traceable anatomical arm; verify chains from shoulders rather than screen-left labels.
Keep a single spearhead, and separate missed defense in beat2 from actual contact reversal in beat3.
Damage should begin at the intended event and persist; avoid preloading a future charred cape into setup.
Use tight threat gaps and body interruption while preserving quiet matte floors.
taste_limit: These observations concern readability and craft, not evidence that the owner likes any image.
